label: Transaction-cost theory of firm boundaries, reading 3 (independent dimensions)

assumptions.statement: Asset specificity is the empirically most important of the three dimensions (s3), a weighting claim revisable in the light of evidence.

propositions.statement: Holding asset specificity constant, including near zero, higher uncertainty raises the probability of vertical integration; the effect of asset specificity is also steeper when uncertainty is high.

assumptions.statement: Uncertainty raises the cost of market governance through adaptation needs even when no specific assets are at stake (surfaced; needed for R15).

note: Frequency (tce:C4) still enters no relation in this reading. The text gives no basis for one, and I did not invent one (see Q5).
